risks.title: Complex Application and Product
risks.question: The product is complicated and complex, developing it may require significant resources, knowledge, and time.
risks.response: Matt has extensive knowledge, and some features are complex but we don't need to develop all complexity first. Can build highly desirable features for lower cost initially. High profit potential far exceeds development cost.
mitigations: Cutting edge technology and AI tools

risks.title: AI Use In Education
risks.question: Will the product increase the use of AI in the classroom by increasing desire to perform and gain rewards?
risks.response: Features can help combat AI use rather than support it. More effort/energy to perform tasks = less likely to use AI. The goal is learning, and product gives students more motivation to try harder.
mitigations: Features for acknowledging and reinforcing non-AI use
More motivation to learn and put effort into assignments

risks.title: Low Performers Gap
risks.question: Does this product increase the gap between low performers and high performers?
risks.response: Product is designed for all users. Low performing students likely receive less positive reinforcement and are more likely to respond positively to it. Specific features can ensure all students receive recognition.
mitigations: Discretely design competitions to ensure all users are recognized

risks.title: School Approval Barrier
risks.question: Can students log in and share data, or is teacher/school approval required?
risks.response: Schools generally need to approve data sharing before students can access LMS tools. This limits direct advertising to students and parents.
risks.impact: Limits direct marketing to students and parents
mitigations: Encourage parents/students to request software approval from schools
Track which schools are requesting access
Large following can make it easier to sell to schools
Broaden outreach beyond just parents and students

risks.title: Integration Difficulty
risks.question: There are many different LMS/SIS systems, some self-hosted. Are there unknown complexities?
risks.response: Ed.Link handles most of this for the United States. Other countries may use different software that may not be supported yet.
risks.impact: US should be fine, some international limitations
mitigations: Deal with missing software as it comes
Work with Ed.Link or build integrations ourselves

risks.title: Ed.Link Integration Stability
risks.question: What happens if Ed.Link sells, goes under, or disappears?
risks.response: Ed.Link is used by many applications including big names and doing well. They've started an integration with Clever. Assuming long-term reliability.
risks.impact: Could be really bad if something happened to the integration platform
mitigations: Can build integrations separately if needed
Only need a few core features, mostly read data
Could switch to supporting only key platforms

risks.title: Privacy, Security, Legal, and Compliance
risks.question: Security and privacy is challenging when handling student data. Countries may have different requirements.
risks.response: Matt has extensive security and privacy career experience from Clever EDU (half of US student data) and LexisNexis Risk Solutions (government identity data). Certifications for SOC, COPPA, FERPA will be needed.
risks.impact: Compliance requirements become necessity, especially for under-13 students
mitigations: Hire additional compliance support as needed
Get compliance certifications as soon as possible
Ed.Link helps with privacy/security for integrations

risks.title: Competition & Mental Health
risks.question: Can competition features negatively impact mental health and add frustration?
risks.response: Benefits outweigh cons. Product designed to promote mental health. Frustration from challenge can be good for engagement when used properly.
mitigations: Abstraction from individual performance using teams, luck, skill, roles

risks.title: Differing Socioeconomic Backgrounds
risks.question: Will certain features be desired by one location and not another? Will money as reward be viewed negatively?
risks.response: Features will be configurable by school. Rewards are customizable and allow users to choose what they want.
mitigations: Feature flags at school, parent, student, teacher, classroom, district, region level
Money may not be primary marketed reward
Let social conversation carry reward details

risks.title: Product Distraction
risks.question: Can the application be distracting in school?
risks.response: This app won't be THE problem. Some classroom usage may be desired. App is designed to improve focus and motivation.

risks.title: Assignment Classification & Data Integrity
risks.question: Can we tell which assignments are tests vs homework? Are grades trustable?
risks.response: Some classifications available, some not. Some misclassified. Some entries are junk or unclear.
mitigations: Design product to count general completion

risks.title: Untested Product
risks.question: The product has not yet been tested so data and proof is missing.
risks.response: Utilize information, emotional appeal, and the need for solution.
risks.impact: Potentially harder entry barrier getting started
mitigations: Keep pushing - it will work out

risks.title: Difficulty Measuring Engagement
risks.question: How do we prove the solution works?
risks.response: Surveys, feedback, statistics on grades/standardized testing/attendance should be sufficient. A/B testing, self-reported mood, attention duration measurements.

risks.title: Gender & Demographic Appeal
risks.question: Does the product appeal to all users? Do males disproportionately benefit?
risks.response: Design is intentionally simple and appeals to all audiences. Psychology base appeals to all users. Girls may prefer social/customization aspects, boys may prefer battles, but girls are often more competitive in education.
mitigations: Target core psychology applying to all humans

risks.title: Ed.Link Feature Limitations
risks.question: Why does Clever LMS Connect not support Blackboard but does support Canvas, Schoology, and Google Classroom?
risks.response: Unknown reasons. Possibly to evaluate potential, build a solution, and consider buyout. Clever is also opening up their API.
mitigations: Clever is opening up API as alternative
Can build direct integrations if needed

risks.title: Integration Pricing for Free Users
risks.question: If we don't know which users will use the software, do we pay for every user even non-users when integrating with schools?
risks.response: Negotiations can be had and pricing is not too bad. Companies are willing to negotiate.
mitigations: Can adjust pricing model if needed

risks.title: Compute & Integration Costs
risks.question: How much will it cost to run syncing and for integrations? How does it impact the business model?
risks.response: Compute is TBD but integrations seem manageable and scale with user base. Ed.Link can negotiate. When compute becomes a cost issue, there will likely be surplus funds.
mitigations: Use events to sync instead of full syncs

risks.title: Syncing & Operational Costs
risks.question: How much does syncing cost, how long does it take, and how frequently can we sync?
risks.response: Current sync for entire school takes a few minutes locally. Many optimization options exist. May not be costly at all.
risks.impact: Each user/school costs some money to operate
mitigations: Optimize based on current compute usage
Run compute locally before cloud scaling

risks.title: Knowledge Gaps in Target Areas
risks.question: Many people don't understand gamification, mental health, engagement, or positive reinforcement deeply.
risks.response: People understand problems exist and basics. They trust figures and data. PBIS is already implemented in many schools, especially higher quality ones.
mitigations: Prove it with data and feedback

risks.title: Password Security for Kids
risks.question: Kids forget passwords or may need easier passwords. How do we handle this?
risks.response: Integration with Clever and other SSO platforms handles this. Can add phone 2FA for higher security features.
mitigations: Required authentication levels based on features used

risks.title: Internationalization & Platform Differences
risks.question: What impact do cultural differences and varying tools/platforms have globally?
risks.response: Much support already exists for global platforms. Many popular LMS/SIS systems are used globally. Can integrate additional platforms as needed.
risks.impact: Need for additional work in future
mitigations: Reward system designed for all cultures (customizable)
Features can be enabled/disabled by region
Cloud hosting in different countries as needed

risks.title: Setup Effort & PM Skills
risks.question: What impact will teachers without good planning/organizational skills have on adoption?
risks.response: Product designed to be as easy as possible to setup with guidance. Beneficial to all teachers and students.

risks.title: Teacher Bias Towards Students
risks.question: If a teacher has positive or negative bias toward certain students, what impact will this have?
risks.response: Bias exists regardless of application. The tool should bring light to these things. More research needed for feature design.
